heroHeadline: ByteDance Raises 2026 AI Capex 25% to $29.4B With Larger Share to Domestic Huawei Chips; Trump-Xi Beijing Summit (May 14–15) Eyes First Formal US-China AI Dialogue
heroSubtitle: ByteDance confirmed on May 9 (Bloomberg/SCMP) that it has raised its 2026 AI infrastructure capex plan by 25% to 200 billion yuan ($29.4 billion) — up from the 160 billion yuan ($22B) plan disclosed in late 2025 — with a 'larger portion of spending now going toward domestic AI chips rather than Nvidia GPUs.' This makes ByteDance one of the top three AI infrastructure spenders globally, behind only Microsoft and Google, and directly confirms that US export controls are accelerating domestic Huawei Ascend procurement at the world's largest token-generation platform: ByteDance's Doubao already logs 120 trillion tokens per day (1,400x growth from January 2024) and is embedded in 7 million vehicles across 50+ car brands. The capex increase aligns with Huawei's Ascend 950PR mass production ramp and ByteDance's existing $5.6B chip commitment. The Trump-Xi Beijing summit scheduled May 14–15 is being considered as the venue for the first formal US-China AI dialogue under the Trump administration — focused on military AI safety, accidental escalation, and non-state actor misuse — though CNBC (May 8) warns Iran nuclear diplomacy is likely to dominate the agenda. Morgan Stanley (May 3) forecast $1.25–1.75B in passive AI inflows to Hong Kong's Hang Seng Tech Index when Zhipu AI and MiniMax join the benchmark on June 8, validating Hong Kong's emergence as China's AI IPO hub after a five-year high of $110B across 40 tech listings in Q1 2026. The 28th Beijing International High-Tech Expo opened May 8 showcasing L4 autonomous vehicles, bionic robotic hands, and AI-eSIM-enabled drones — confirming that China's physical AI deployment is no longer prototype but commercially operational across sectors. Structural picture as of May 9, 2026: ByteDance ($29.4B AI capex, domestic chips), Huawei (60% AI chip market, $12B revenue target), DeepSeek ($45B valuation, Big Fund-led), SMIC ($9.33B revenue, Q1 results May 14), MiniMax (#4 globally), and China's tech stocks at all-time highs — every layer of China's AI stack continues accelerating simultaneously as the Trump-Xi summit approaches.
